title: Partition Labels
description:
# Partition Labels

You are given a string `s` of lowercase English letters. Partition `s` into as many non-empty contiguous parts as possible so that every letter appears in at most one part.

After concatenating the parts in order, the result must be exactly the original string `s`.

Return a list of integers representing the length of each part.

## Example 1:

**Input:** s = "ababcbacadefegdehijhklij"
**Output:** [9,7,8]
**Explanation:** The partition is "ababcbaca", "defegde", "hijhklij". Each letter appears in only one part, and this is the maximum possible number of parts.

## Example 2:

**Input:** s = "eccbbbbdec"
**Output:** [10]
**Explanation:** The last `e` and the last `c` force every character into one part.

## Example 3:

**Input:** s = "caedbdedda"
**Output:** [1,9]
**Explanation:** The leading `c` closes immediately. The remaining letters overlap through their later occurrences.

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= s.length <= 500`
*   `s` consists of lowercase English letters.

solutions.name: Greedy with Last Occurrence Map
solutions.description:
## Approach
Record the last index of every character. Scan from left to right while extending the current partition end to the farthest last occurrence of any character seen in the partition. When the scan index reaches that end, emit the partition length.

## Key Insight
A partition cannot close before the last occurrence of any character it already contains. Closing at the first index where all seen characters have ended gives the shortest valid current part, which leaves the most remaining space for future parts.

## Complexity Analysis
The string is scanned twice and the alphabet has fixed size 26, so the time complexity is O(n). The last-occurrence array and output aside use O(1) extra space.

solutions.name: Merge Character Intervals
solutions.description:
## Approach
For each character that appears, build the interval from its first occurrence to its last occurrence. Sort those character intervals by start position and merge overlaps. Every merged interval is one valid partition.

## Key Insight
All occurrences of the same character must stay in one part, so each character creates a required interval. If two required intervals overlap, their characters must share a partition. The final answer is exactly the list of merged interval lengths.

## Complexity Analysis
Let `k` be the number of distinct characters, at most 26 here. Building intervals takes O(n), sorting them takes O(k log k), and merging takes O(k). The interval list uses O(k) extra space.

solutions.name: Remaining Frequency Active Set
solutions.description:
## Approach
Count the remaining occurrences of every character. During the scan, keep an active set of characters that have appeared in the current partition but still occur later. A partition closes exactly when that active set becomes empty.

## Key Insight
Instead of storing last positions, this method stores the same obligation dynamically: a character keeps the current partition open until its remaining count drops to zero. When no active character remains, no future character is tied to the current part.

## Complexity Analysis
Counting and scanning are both linear, so the time complexity is O(n). The remaining counts and active flags are fixed arrays of length 26, so the extra space is O(1).

solutions.name: Brute Force Closed-Segment Check
solutions.description:
## Approach
Precompute each character's first and last occurrence. Starting from the next unpartitioned index, try candidate end positions from left to right and choose the first segment that fully contains every character interval it touches.

## Key Insight
A segment is valid if every character either has all of its occurrences inside the segment or has no occurrence inside it. Testing this condition directly is slower, but it is a useful correctness baseline because it mirrors the problem statement literally.

## Complexity Analysis
For each start position, the method may test many end positions, and each test checks 26 characters, so the time complexity is O(26 * n^2). The first and last arrays are fixed size, so the extra space is O(1).

solutions.name: Union-Find Index Components
solutions.description:
## Approach
Compute each character interval, then union all indices inside each interval with that interval's first index. After all unions, scan the string and output the lengths of contiguous connected components.

## Key Insight
Every index between the first and last occurrence of a character is forced into the same final part. Overlapping character intervals become connected components, and each component corresponds to exactly one partition.

## Complexity Analysis
There are at most 26 character intervals, and each interval may union a linear number of indices, so the time complexity is O(26 * n α(n)). The disjoint-set structure stores one parent per index, so the space complexity is O(n).

tests.description: Canonical sample with three maximal labels.
Overlapping first and last occurrences force the whole string into one part.
All same character forces one partition.
Two repeated letters overlap across the whole string.
Repeated pattern keeps all letters in one partition.
Leading singleton closes before a long overlapping suffix.
A repeated first letter closes the first segment, then a singleton remains.
Nested pair interval followed by a short repeated block and a singleton.
A first partition, a middle singleton, and a mirrored suffix partition.
Two independent nested groups should not be merged together.
